title: Causal Masking in the Transformer Decoder

diagram.title: Causal masking before softmax
diagram.caption: Across six positions, add $M_{ij}=-\infty$ when $j>i$ and $0$ otherwise. Gray cells show the blocked scores.

body:
To prevent future leakage, the decoder applies a causal mask directly to the attention scores before computing the softmax normalisation.

Look at the heatmap to see how future positions receive negative infinity values that completely block information flow.

By setting $M_{ij} = -\infty$ for all key positions $j$ greater than query position $i$, the model forces those specific attention weights to zero.

This ensures that during autoregressive generation, each token can only attend to past and present tokens in the sequence.
questions: What happens to the softmax output when all future scores are set to negative infinity?
Why is causal masking unnecessary in standard transformer encoder blocks?
How does KV caching interact with causal masking during inference?

terms.d: A matrix added to attention scores in a decoder to prevent tokens from attending to subsequent tokens.
An activation function that normalizes a vector of scores into a probability distribution summing to one.
